23080.overview: CD-I makes Tangram more challenging, more exciting. There are more symbols, more silhouettes, so you can develop greater skills. Just use the cursor to rotate and move the pieces. Choose free expression or tackle set tasks. And choose your own level of play: beginner, intermediate, advanced, expert - up to the highest level of all. Free Form Tangram on CD-I means moving forms, mood music, and much more fun!

23081.overview:
Tetris... a classic game in a class of its own. Originally conceived by Alexey Pazhitnov and designed by Vadim Gerasimov of the former USSR, Tetris is recognized all over the world for its elegant simplicity and challenging game play.

Tetris CD-i is the ultimate Tetris experience. Spectacular video nature scenes and an original CD score by Jim Andron complement classic Tetris game play and elevate this phenomenon to new heights. In CD-i, the classic becomes a legend.

You'll find Tetris CD-i irresistibly addicting as you try to rotate and flip moving pieces to fit into a solid line at the bottom of the playing field. Remove ten lines and you move on to the next level! Discover what game players all over the world have learned...this is one addiction you can't live without.

- Original Tetris Game Play features
- Ten levels of play
- Spectacular motion video nature backgrounds
- Ten original CD soundtracks

23082.overview:
Tetsuo Gaiden, a fantasy flight through the realms of alien darkness. Featuring the best CD-i has got to offer; amazing 3D full motion video, riveting gameplay and a smack in your face soundtrack...

Prepare for more than 80 blazing levels filled with the best and fastest gameplay ever created on CD-i. Brought to you by the award-winning team from Christmas Country, Tetsuo Gaiden is jampacked with nice features like bonus items, multiple laser fire, smartbombs, energy shields and super bonusses.

Get ready for the best game of spring '97.

23083.overview: Text Tiles is a strategic puzzle game in which players have to spell words. Using a set of given letters the players have to form words, much like Scrabble. This is done on a 12x12 board. The letters can be used to either form a long word or multiple short words. Points are scored for each correct word. Letters are received one at a time and disappear again after a certain amount of time creating a time pressure for forming words. The player can see what his next letter is going to be so he can plan ahead. The game can be played with up to four players.

23092.overview: Here's your shot at Paradise, bro. You're in the middle of an action-packed adventure with your cohorts Spence (Terry "Hulk" Hogan) and Bru (Chris Lemmon). Blast your way through these mind-blowing action encounters as you attempt to rescue Spence's daughter Jessica, regain control of the M.A.J.O.R., and crush your arch enemy, RAMPIKE! Race at hyperspeed through the Caribbean, aboard THUNDER, a 45-foot piece of hi-tech marine hardware. Take control of the boat's weapon systems and defend THUNDER from a shower of deadly threats. Face down minions of the psychotic RAMPIKE on the eerie trails of Rossiter's Island. Go toe-to-toe with the M.A.J.O.R., a bio-humanoid gone haywire, in a battle for Jessica's life!

23150.overview: Tic Tac Toe is a basic implementation of original paper and pencil version. The player may compete only with computer. The game is entirely keyboard controlled by pressing 1-9 buttons, assigned to one field on the board.

23164.overview: Titanic: An Interactive Exploration was essentially an interactive documentary released for Phillip's illfated CDI platform.

23175.overview: Tell Me Why One is an interactive trivia game. There are over 175 questions that need answering. Questions in the game are typical questions that curious children might ask. They come in five categories: our world, how things work, the zoo, how things began and the human body. Questions are supported with audio and visuals. The game comes with over 3 hours of fact filled presentations and interactive exhibits.

23176.overview: Tell Me Why Two is an interactive trivia game and sequel to Tell Me Why One. The game comes with an additional 175+ questions that need answering. Questions in the game are typical questions that curious children might ask. They come in five categories: our world, how things work, the zoo, how things began and the human body. Questions are supported with audio and visuals. The game comes with over 3 hours of fact filled presentations and interactive exhibits.

194254.overview: Le journal interactif 94 et Le jeu des stars de l'info is a collection of newsreels from the French broadcast company TF1. In this multimedia title you can review all the news subject of 1994. You can also create your own news show using footage from the same year. The goal is to to impress the chief editor.

194261.overview:
Thumbelina is an interactive telling of the story by Hans Christian Andersen. It features video fragments and stills from the cartoon film by Don Bluth. As the story is told images are show in the background. Many of these images include activities. These activities include coloring, starting animations through clicking on hot-spots and simple puzzles like counting objects and moving shapes to the correct sockets with the cursor.

Colored images start to animate once they are filled in. The whole story is divided into seven chapters, so that it is possible to skip to the activities you want to play, or continue the story at a different time.

194262.overview:
Tom: Magic Picture Show is an educational game for children ages 2 and up. In the game they can learn English, French or German through a variety of activities.

Activities include various puzzle games and a coloring book. The whole game is accompanied with a soundtrack.

194263.overview:
Unlike the first title in the series which didn't feature interaction (beyond choosing which of the two characters to follow), this second Tim & Beer title is fully interactive.

Tim and his teddy bear are visiting their cousin Tina who lives far away. Because of this they have to go by plane. Of course it's not easy to navigate around an airport.

Tim & Bear at the Airport is an interactive cartoon film in which the viewer watches Tim & Beer explore the airport and the airplane. Viewers can opt to let the cartoon roll, or at times interfere and tell Tim or Bear what to do by choosing from several preset options. This creates tiny differences in how the story progresses.

194264.overview:
Tim & Bear at the Movies is the fourth part in the series. After having flown to their cousin Tina and having visited the harbor, Tim and Bear return with the airplane, but through accident end up in a movie development studio.

The game is an interactive cartoon film in which the viewer watches Tim & Bear explore the movie studio. Viewers can opt to let the cartoon roll, or at times interfere and tell Tim or Bear what to do by choosing from several preset options. This creates tiny differences in how the story progresses.

420480.overview: This title is part of Philips Media’s School 2000 Project.

420490.overview: Tim and Bear at the Harbour is the third program in the Tim and Bear series.  Tim and Bear go to visit their cousin, tina, and Uncle Bob.  They are all going to visit Uncle Bob’s old boat, which is lying in the harbour.  This boat cannot be used, because the propeller has been lost.  They decide to all go and look for the propeller has been lost.

420496.overview:
Interactive television finally within the reach of all. Consult the Journal of the Year 1995 according to your wishes thanks to the more than one hour of full screen video: all the strong images of TF1 news. The great journalists of the chain present this year 1995 and accompany you to better understand the news.
A great family game made in full screen video! From 1 to 4 players, 150 reports, more than 750 questions and the surprises of Clair Chazal, Jean-Pierre Pernaut, Roland Thierry, Roger Zabel, Michel Chevalet …

447249.overview:
24 mini-games with adjustable difficulty!
Save a separate experience for up to six members of your family!
Original animation and voices!
Featuring the voice of Diana Ross as Glenda the good witch!
Relive the classic on the Philips CD-I!
